eli5.text: Windows users running Codebuff may now see a new error message, "Bash is required but was not found", if their system lacks a compatible bash shell. The software has switched from using the built-in Windows command processor to requiring bash, which it searches for in your system's PATH, common Git for Windows install locations, or a custom path you can set. If bash cannot be found, Codebuff stops and shows setup instructions instead of running commands; installing Git for Windows or using WSL resolves it. This change is live today for anyone running Codebuff on Windows.

ai.title: Fix CLI message queue race and add --wait-idle to tmux
ai.summary: Refactored `useMessageQueue` to perform atomic state updates inside `setQueuedMessages`, preventing race conditions where the processed message mismatched the removed one. The `Chat` component switched to `useLayoutEffect` for context updates to ensure synchronous rendering during rapid streaming. The `tmux-send.sh` harness gained `--wait-idle SECS` and `--delay MS` flags to reliably detect stream completion and adjust post-enter timing in automated tests.

eli5.text: The CLI now sends messages in the correct order more reliably, even when you send several quickly and your terminal is still streaming a response. Behind the scenes, the message queue was reworked so it always removes and sends the same message together (no more mismatched send/remove race), and context updates during streaming now happen synchronously. If you use the tmux test harness, you can now pass --wait-idle SECS to make it pause until the terminal output is stable before returning, and --delay MS to control how long to wait after pressing Enter. These changes are live today.

ai.title: SDK run-terminal-command prefers Git Bash over WSL bash
ai.summary: Windows bash resolution in `sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts` now prioritizes `GIT_BASH_COMMON_PATHS` and non-WSL `PATH` entries before falling back to WSL. `WSL_BASH_PATH_PATTERNS` (`system32`, `windowsapps`) identify unreliable WSL paths, deferring them to last-resort fallbacks. WSL bash remains supported but is deprioritized to avoid failures when the VM is inactive or due to Windows/Linux quoting and UTF-16 encoding mismatches.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to run a command in a terminal on Windows, it now looks for Git Bash first and treats Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) Bash as a backup option. Previously the order could mix WSL and Git Bash together, sometimes picking WSL even when it wasn't running, leading to confusing errors. Now reliable Git Bash installations are checked before any WSL Bash found on the system path, and WSL Bash is only used if nothing else is available. If you look closely, you'd notice the program tries your standard Git Bash setup before falling back to the WSL version.

ai.summary: Freebuff 1.0.588 rolls up a dense day of CLI and SDK improvements. The CLI help banner now advertises Ctrl+J and Option+Enter as newline shortcuts and consolidates @files and @agents references, while the message queue was made race-free via atomic updates in useMessageQueue and a tmux-send.sh harness gain. ai.title: Improve Discord advisory lock reliability for leader election
ai.summary: Advisory lock implementation in `packages/internal/src/db/advisory-lock.ts` now returns a `LockHandle` object instead of a raw `postgres.Sql` connection. This handle exposes `onLost()` callbacks and a `release()` method, with an internal 30-second health check interval to detect connection drops. `web/scripts/discord/index.ts` consumes this new API, adding error handling for lock acquisition failures and a `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS` limit (5) before exiting. The `releaseAdvisoryLock` export was removed from `packages/internal/src/db/index.ts`.

eli5.text: When you start the Discord assistant, it now checks every 30 seconds that it is still the leader holding the lock; if the database connection drops, it gives up the lock immediately instead of waiting. The bot will retry up to five times before stopping if it cannot acquire the lock, and it cleans up the Discord connection and releases the lock before exiting. If you look at a running bot, it will shut down cleanly when asked and report a clear error if the lock fails too many times in a row. This is live for the internal Discord bot today.
